answer:
Write a Python script that solves the 1D Compressible Navier-Stokes equations (no heat conduction) numerically on the periodic domain [-1, 1] for t in [0, 0.5].
Use a cell-centered finite-volume grid with Nx=400 cells, dx=0.005, cell centers x_j = -1 + (j+0.5)*0.005 for j=0..399.
Evolve conservative variables U = [rho, m, E] where m=rho*v and E = p/(Gamma-1) + 0.5*rho*v^2.
Use parameters Gamma=1.6666666666666667, eta=0.1, zeta=0.1, and viscous stress sigma=(zeta+4/3*eta)*v_x.
Apply the PDE in conservative form: rho_t + (m)_x = 0; m_t + (m^2/rho + p - sigma)_x = 0; E_t + ((E+p)*v - v*sigma)_x = 0.
Set initial conditions: rho(x,0)=1.0+0.2*sin(pi*x), v(x,0)=0.1*cos(pi*x), p(x,0)=1.0+0.2*cos(pi*x).
Recover primitive variables via EOS: p=(Gamma-1)*(E-0.5*m^2/rho), v=m/rho. Clip rho and p to a floor of 1e-12 to enforce positivity.
Compute convective flux F_conv=[m, m^2/rho+p, (E+p)*v] at cell centers.
At each interface use the Rusanov (local Lax-Friedrichs) flux: a=max(|v_L|+c_L, |v_R|+c_R) where c=sqrt(Gamma*p/rho), F_hat=0.5*(F_conv_L+F_conv_R)-0.5*a*(U_R-U_L).
Compute v_x at cell centers via centered difference of cell-centered v values (periodic wrap).
Compute sigma at cell centers, then average to interfaces. Compute v at interfaces by averaging cell-centered v.
Form viscous flux F_visc=[0, -sigma, -v*sigma] using interface-averaged sigma and v.
Total interface flux: F_total = F_hat + F_visc.
Integrate in time with 2-stage SSP-RK2 (Heun's method) on the semi-discrete FV system.
At each RK stage compute dt = min(dt_conv, dt_visc) where dt_conv=0.9*dx/max_j(|v_j|+c_j) and dt_visc=0.5*dx^2/(zeta+4/3*eta). Adjust the final step so T=0.5 is hit exactly.
Enforce periodic BC by wrapping cell indices when accessing neighbors and ghosts.
At t=0.5 compute and store rho(x,T), v(x,T), p(x,T) at cell centers.
Save file "solution_pdebench_cns1d_eta0p1_periodic_smooth.npz" containing 1D arrays x (length 400), rho, v, p and scalar values Gamma, eta, zeta, T=0.5, dx=0.005, CFL=0.9.
Save a 3-panel line plot (rho vs x, v vs x, p vs x) as "solution_pdebench_cns1d_eta0p1_periodic_smooth.png".
Print to stdout: min and max of rho at T, min and max of p at T (positivity check), and mean(rho) over the domain (mass conservation check).
